01 · Jets

Observing QCD

Experiments measure hadrons, not partons

e+e−e^+e^-e+e− collide and make a hard parton pair at d∼1/s≪1/ΛQCDd\sim1/\sqrt s\ll1/\Lambda_{\rm QCD}d∼1/s​≪1/ΛQCD​: perturbation theory works.

The parton shower: repeated splittings, dP∼αs2πPqq(z)dθ2θ2dzdP\sim\frac{\alpha_s}{2\pi}P_{qq}(z)\frac{d\theta^2}{\theta^2}dzdP∼2παs​​Pqq​(z)θ2dθ2​dz, enhanced at small angle and small energy.

At d∼1/ΛQCDd\sim1/\Lambda_{\rm QCD}d∼1/ΛQCD​ hadronization turns coloured partons into colourless hadrons: non-perturbative.

The detector sees hadrons. A jet is a group of them that we cluster to recover the hard parton.

d∼1/s≪1/ΛQCDd\sim 1/\sqrt s\ll 1/\Lambda_{\rm QCD}d∼1/s​≪1/ΛQCD​
dP∼αs2π Pqq(z) dθ2θ2 dzdP\sim\dfrac{\alpha_s}{2\pi}\,P_{qq}(z)\,\dfrac{d\theta^2}{\theta^2}\,dzdP∼2παs​​Pqq​(z)θ2dθ2​dz
d∼1/ΛQCDd\sim 1/\Lambda_{\rm QCD}d∼1/ΛQCD​

01 · Jets

Jets and IRC safety

Jets are defined by clustering algorithms

Clustering: nearby particles are merged into pJ=∑i∈Jpip_J=\sum_{i\in J}p_ipJ​=∑i∈J​pi​.
dij=min⁡ ⁣(pT,i2p,pT,j2p)ΔRij2R2,diB=pT,i2pd_{ij}=\min\!\big(p_{T,i}^{2p},p_{T,j}^{2p}\big)\frac{\Delta R_{ij}^2}{R^2},\quad d_{iB}=p_{T,i}^{2p}dij​=min(pT,i2p​,pT,j2p​)R2ΔRij2​​,diB​=pT,i2p​
p=1p=1p=1: kTk_TkT​ · p=0p=0p=0: Aachen · p=−1p=-1p=−1: anti-kTk_TkT​
There is no unique jet definition: the reconstructed jets depend on the clustering prescription.

Only IRC safe observables are computable in perturbation theory: soft and collinear emissions, which no detector can resolve, must not change the answer (otherwise the QCD singularities do not cancel).

01 · Jets

Jet observables: charge and flavor tagging

The parity-odd combination A−BA-BA−B needs quark versus antiquark

Charge tagging. Jet charge, a momentum-weighted sum, statistically correlated with the quark charge (with mistag):
QJ(κ)=∑i∈JQi ∣pi,∥∣κ∑i∈J∣pi,∥∣κ\mathcal Q_J^{(\kappa)}=\frac{\sum_{i\in J}Q_i\,|p_{i,\parallel}|^\kappa}{\sum_{i\in J}|p_{i,\parallel}|^\kappa}QJ(κ)​=∑i∈J​∣pi,∥​∣κ∑i∈J​Qi​∣pi,∥​∣κ​
Flavor tagging. Heavy quarks form hadrons that keep the flavor, and long lifetimes give displaced vertices: q=b,cq=b,cq=b,c.
Forward–backward asymmetry:

02

Flow operators

Energy and charge correlators at null infinity

Can we build observables that are sensitive to the difference between quarks and antiquarks, without identifying their jets individually?

02 · Correlators

Exciting the QCD vacuum

The QCD vacuum ∣0⟩|0\rangle∣0⟩: strongly coupled and fluctuating. There are no particles to look at.

Excite it with the current: Jμ(0)∣0⟩=∑X∣X⟩⟨X∣Jμ(0)∣0⟩J^\mu(0)|0\rangle=\sum_X|X\rangle\langle X|J^\mu(0)|0\rangleJμ(0)∣0⟩=∑X​∣X⟩⟨X∣Jμ(0)∣0⟩. Not a single hadron: a superposition of multi-hadron states XXX, with pX=qp_X=qpX​=q after the Fourier transform.

Shower and hadronization turn qqˉq\bar qqqˉ​ into many hadrons.

Instead of grouping particles into jets, imagine placing ideal detectors very far from the collision point. Every hadron crosses a sphere at null infinity:  D(n^)∣X⟩=∑idi δ(2)(Ωn^−Ωi)∣X⟩,  di=Ei, qi, Bi\ \mathcal D(\hat n)|X\rangle=\sum_i d_i\,\delta^{(2)}(\Omega_{\hat n}-\Omega_i)|X\rangle,\ \ d_i=E_i,\,q_i,\,B_i D(n^)∣X⟩=∑i​di​δ(2)(Ωn^​−Ωi​)∣X⟩,  di​=Ei​,qi​,Bi​

Average over events: energy flow is even in cos⁡θ\cos\thetacosθ, charge flow is odd: it sees the parity-odd coefficient A−BA-BA−B.

⟨E(cos⁡θ)⟩  ∝  1+cos⁡2θ\langle\mathcal E(\cos\theta)\rangle\;\propto\;1+\cos^2\theta⟨E(cosθ)⟩∝1+cos2θ
⟨Q(cos⁡θ)⟩  ∝  (A−B)cos⁡θ\langle\mathcal Q(\cos\theta)\rangle\;\propto\;(A-B)\cos\theta⟨Q(cosθ)⟩∝(A−B)cosθ
Flow operators

Flow operators: no jet algorithm

02 · Correlators

From CFT to QCD

Why the same operators make sense in QCD, and what changes

⟨O† E(n^1)⋯E(n^N) O⟩  ⟶  ⟨J† D(n^1)⋯D(n^N) J⟩\langle\mathcal O^\dagger\,\mathcal E(\hat n_1)\cdots\mathcal E(\hat n_N)\,\mathcal O\rangle\;\longrightarrow\;\langle J^\dagger\,\mathcal D(\hat n_1)\cdots\mathcal D(\hat n_N)\,J\rangle⟨O†E(n^1​)⋯E(n^N​)O⟩⟶⟨J†D(n^1​)⋯D(n^N​)J⟩

CFT

Source: any local primary O\mathcal OO. Detectors: light-ray integrals of TμνT_{\mu\nu}Tμν​.

Conformal symmetry fixes correlators up to a few OPE data. No scale, no running.

Positivity of the detectors (ANEC) bounds the data.

QCD

Why it works: E,Q,B\mathcal E,\mathcal Q,\mathcal BE,Q,B only need conserved currents and massless asymptotic states. The source is the electroweak current JJJ. Conformality is not required.

What changes: running αs\alpha_sαs​, confinement, masses. The numbers that multiply each angular structure depend on s\sqrt ss​ and on hadronization.

What stays: rotations (spin-1 source), positivity, IRC safety, the light-ray OPE in the collinear limit.

Symmetry fixes the shape of the correlator; dynamics fixes its coefficients.

Hadronization

Safe is not hadronization-free

Symmetry fixes the angular form; hadronization changes only the coefficients

IRC safe means finite order by order in αs\alpha_sαs​, not independent of the non-perturbative physics: hadronization rescales the coefficients CEC_{\mathcal E}CE​, CQC_{\mathcal Q}CQ​.
LO has the right shape but the wrong coefficient; Pythia reproduces the data.
Strategy: LO shape ×\times× coefficient fitted on the Monte Carlo, which is validated on LEP data.

Contact interactions between electrons and the uuu quark

Conclusions

Conclusions

01
Flow observables are one of the most natural ways to describe what we observe at colliders.
02
They satisfy nice properties such as IRC safety.
03
The structure of the correlators is fixed by symmetries; the coefficients receive perturbative corrections (safe) and non-perturbative effects.
04
Charge flow gives the parity-odd coupling combination without jets or flavour tagging, where energy is blind to it.
05
Z pole: reach comparable to flavour-tagged jets, and it extends to light quarks.
06
BSM: four-fermion contact operators gain a new direction from ⟨Q⟩\langle\mathcal Q\rangle⟨Q⟩.
07
Correlators are crucial where different helicities matter: done for the semileptonic WWWWWW analysis at LEP2, for the TGCs.
08
Many people are working on this topic. Work in progress with Monni: analytic non-perturbative effects for the EQ\mathcal{EQ}EQ back-to-back configuration.

Why charge flow needs no jet and no flavour tag

The forward-backward asymmetry with jets vs with a detector at a point

Jets, untagged. A jet axis has no orientation: θ\thetaθ and π−θ\pi-\thetaπ−θ are the same event. 12[σ(c)+σ(−c)]=(A+B)(1+c2)\tfrac12\big[\sigma(c)+\sigma(-c)\big]=(A+B)(1+c^2)21​[σ(c)+σ(−c)]=(A+B)(1+c2) A−BA-BA−B drops out. To keep it we must tag the sign (which jet is the quark, e.g. jet charge) and, for AFBuA_{FB}^uAFBu​, also the flavour.
Charge flow. The detector sits at a fixed point n^\hat nn^ and measures a signed quantity: the quark brings +Qq+Q_q+Qq​ to n^\hat nn^, the antiquark −Qq-Q_q−Qq​. ⟨Q(n^)⟩∝Qq[σ(c)−σ(−c)]∝Qq(A−B) c\langle\mathcal Q(\hat n)\rangle\propto Q_q\big[\sigma(c)-\sigma(-c)\big]\propto Q_q(A-B)\,c⟨Q(n^)⟩∝Qq​[σ(c)−σ(−c)]∝Qq​(A−B)c The charge is the sign tag. No jet, no event-by-event flavour tag.

Summed over all flavours: CQ∝∑qQq(A(q)−B(q))C_{\mathcal Q}\propto\sum_qQ_q\big(A^{(q)}-B^{(q)}\big)CQ​∝∑q​Qq​(A(q)−B(q)), a charge-weighted forward-backward asymmetry of the whole hadronic sample.

c=cos⁡θc=\cos\thetac=cosθ, θ\thetaθ between n^\hat nn^ and the e−e^-e− beam. σ(c)=A(1+c)2+B(1−c)2\sigma(c)=A(1+c)^2+B(1-c)^2σ(c)=A(1+c)2+B(1−c)2. Energy flow is even, so like untagged jets it only sees A+BA+BA+B.

Why the back-to-back ⟨EQ⟩\langle\mathcal{EQ}\rangle⟨EQ⟩ is IRC safe

Energy detector on the qqq spray, charge detector on the qˉ\bar qqˉ​ spray

Why it is IRC safe. Back to back, the event is two opposite sprays of particles: one started by the qqq, one by the qˉ\bar qqˉ​.
• Energy detector on the qqq spray: it collects the energy of the spray, always s/2\sqrt s/2s​/2, however it fragments.
• Charge detector on the qˉ\bar qqˉ​ spray: charge is conserved, so the spray carries the charge of the qˉ\bar qqˉ​ that started it. 2Eq-sprays  Qqˉ-spray=Qqˉ\frac{2E_{q\text{-spray}}}{\sqrt s}\;Q_{\bar q\text{-spray}}=Q_{\bar q}s​2Eq-spray​​Qqˉ​-spray​=Qqˉ​​ Shower and hadronization only redistribute what is conserved. What is left is perturbative recoil (TMD jet functions), with Sudakov logs near z→1z\to1z→1.

Jets and IRC safety: full argument

Jets are defined by clustering algorithms; IRC safety makes them compatible with QCD singularities

Clustering: nearby particles are merged into pJ=∑i∈Jpip_J=\sum_{i\in J}p_ipJ​=∑i∈J​pi​.
dij=min⁡ ⁣(pT,i2p,pT,j2p)ΔRij2R2,diB=pT,i2pd_{ij}=\min\!\big(p_{T,i}^{2p},p_{T,j}^{2p}\big)\frac{\Delta R_{ij}^2}{R^2},\quad d_{iB}=p_{T,i}^{2p}dij​=min(pT,i2p​,pT,j2p​)R2ΔRij2​​,diB​=pT,i2p​
p=1p=1p=1: kTk_TkT​ · p=0p=0p=0: Aachen · p=−1p=-1p=−1: anti-kTk_TkT​
There is no unique jet definition: the reconstructed jets depend on the clustering prescription.

Why we need IRC safety: soft and collinear emissions are not under perturbative control and not resolved by a detector. An observable that depends on them cannot be compared with a calculation.

Infrared safety: O({pi},k)→k→0O({pi})\mathcal O(\{p_i\},k)\xrightarrow{k\to0}\mathcal O(\{p_i\})O({pi​},k)k→0​O({pi​}). An infinitely soft particle changes nothing.
Collinear safety: O(…,pi,pj,… )→pi∥pjO(…,pi+pj,… )\mathcal O(\dots,p_i,p_j,\dots)\xrightarrow{p_i\parallel p_j}\mathcal O(\dots,p_i+p_j,\dots)O(…,pi​,pj​,…)pi​∥pj​​O(…,pi​+pj​,…).

KLN theorem: for IRC safe observables the soft and collinear divergences of virtual and real emissions cancel: the result is finite order by order (diagrams in backup).

Bootstrapping flow operators

In a CFT the detectors are light-ray operators, and their OPE is bootstrappable

⟨E(n^1)E(n^2)⟩⟨E(n^1)⟩⟨E(n^2)⟩=∑OλϕTO2  GO(z),z=1−n^1 ⁣⋅n^22\frac{\langle\mathcal E(\hat n_1)\mathcal E(\hat n_2)\rangle}{\langle\mathcal E(\hat n_1)\rangle\langle\mathcal E(\hat n_2)\rangle}=\sum_{\mathcal O}\lambda^2_{\phi T\mathcal O}\;G_{\mathcal O}(z),\qquad z=\frac{1-\hat n_1\!\cdot\hat n_2}{2}⟨E(n^1​)⟩⟨E(n^2​)⟩⟨E(n^1​)E(n^2​)⟩​=O∑​λϕTO2​GO​(z),z=21−n^1​⋅n^2​​
Light-ray OPE. E×E\mathcal E\times\mathcal EE×E expands in light-ray operators (J=3J=3J=3 family). The expansion is non-perturbative and convergent; GOG_{\mathcal O}GO​ are celestial blocks, the coefficients are local CFT data.
Result 1: conformal collider bounds. ⟨E⟩∝1+a2(cos⁡2θ−13)≥0\langle\mathcal E\rangle\propto1+a_2(\cos^2\theta-\tfrac13)\ge0⟨E⟩∝1+a2​(cos2θ−31​)≥0 gives −32≤a2≤3-\tfrac32\le a_2\le3−23​≤a2​≤3, i.e. 12≤ac≤32\tfrac12\le\tfrac ac\le\tfrac3221​≤ca​≤23​ for N=1\mathcal N=1N=1 SCFTs. Proven for any unitary CFT: 13≤ac≤3118\tfrac13\le\tfrac ac\le\tfrac{31}{18}31​≤ca​≤1831​.
Result 2: EEC in N=4\mathcal N=4N=4 SYM. The celestial block expansion reproduces weak and strong coupling and predicts the EEC through 4 loops.
In QCD: a free quark pair sits exactly at the lower bound a2=−32a_2=-\tfrac32a2​=−23​; αs\alpha_sαs​ moves it inside. The light-ray OPE controls the collinear limit; a full bootstrap needs conformality.

Why no tagging? With jets, AFBA_{FB}AFB​ needs to know which jet is the quark: unlabelled, dσd\sigmadσ is symmetrized to (A+B)(1+cos⁡2θ)(A+B)(1+\cos^2\theta)(A+B)(1+cos2θ) and A−BA-BA−B is lost. The charge detector orients the event by itself, since qqq and qˉ\bar qqˉ​ have opposite charge. Summed over all flavours with weight QqQ_qQq​: a charge-weighted AFBA_{FB}AFB​ of the whole hadronic sample.
